description: PLACE KEEPER RESERVE, built and held off: the holder signs a record that names one keeper wallet, a cap in NET units, an end date and one place (kept only as a 350 metre cell), or revokes their own record. It is a record only: it binds no one, nothing is held, sent or paid, no keeper can act under it yet, you can spend the NET or revoke the record at any time, and it gives nobody any right in any land or site. The kind of place, public ground or private, is your own word and nothing here checks it. The door checks the cap against your wallet's fresh NET balance less the NET the wallet has already named in other records. The work itself is posted, claimed, proven and accepted on the board by other people. You name one act: sign (the holder, the keeper's 0x address, a cap in whole NET units, the day the record lapses, a pin and whether the place is public ground or private, the upkeep meant in a plain sentence, and optionally which acts the keeper may prepare), or revoke (the holder ends their own record). A keeper may prepare a plan, a link or a renewal only; it can never sign for you, pay anyone, post a job or accept anyone's work. FREE to sign, no fee, no gas. The program is built but held off until the operator switches it on: until then a new record is refused before you sign, with the same answer whatever you send, and a revocation only works on a record that exists, even while the NET programs are stopped. What depends on this wallet is answered only when you submit, so prepare never says whether a wallet holds a record: the cap of five open records for one wallet, whether the wallet's balance covers the cap (a balance that cannot be read is refused there too), an id already in use with other terms, and a revocation by a wallet that did not make the record. If one applies, nothing is recorded, and each is refused after the signature is verified, so each spends the signature. Prepare refuses only what is true for every wallet: a body that breaks the door's rules and a house wallet as the holder or the keeper. This moves no NET, and the house pays, holds and sells nothing through these tools. Never put a phone number, an email, a street address or a place name in any field. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the holder wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_place_keeper within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

act.description: sign records a new record, or revoke ends one you hold.

actions.description: sign, optional: which acts the keeper may prepare, from plan_commission, link_packet and renew_commission. Left out, all three.

expiresAt.description: sign: the day the record lapses, an ISO time at least 7 days and at most 366 days from now.

keeper.description: sign: the 0x… address of the one wallet you name to coordinate the upkeep, a different wallet from yours. Address only.

mandateId.description: The record's id: 1 to 80 letters, numbers and . _ : -. You choose it when you sign; the same id and the same terms read the record back.

place.description: sign: { lat, lng }, the place's pin. Only its 350 metre cell is kept; send no name and no address.

placeKind.description: sign: public_ground or private. It is your own word and nothing checks it; a private place is never shown on any read.

principal.description: The 0x… address that signs: the wallet that holds the record. Address only, never a private key.

reason.description: revoke: optional, one plain sentence, up to 280 characters. Only you ever read it back.

scope.description: sign: the upkeep you mean, one plain sentence of 10 to 200 characters. No contact details, no address, no violation words and no words that read as a right in land.

units.description: sign: the cap, in whole NET units, at least 1 (1 NET is 1,000,000 units). It is your own number, never filled in for you.

name: prepare_net_place_keeper
title: Sign or revoke a place keeper record: name one keeper wallet, a NET cap and an end date for one place (step 1 of 2)
